title: A Little Girl with Blue Hair
paragraphs: What a heavy atmosphere is starting to take hold here.
“Well, if the Dragon King shows up alone, I could take it down by myself.”
Father almost slips and falls. Everyone around him has a similar reaction. Did I say something strange?
“We can win… Why didn’t you say so sooner?”
“Back then, a series of misfortunes piled up like a domino effect.”

Ren and Itsuki went and broke the seals on the Spirit Tortoise and the Phoenix on their own, and on top of that, Takt refused to be persuaded and attacked us—and that’s what triggered the appearance of the Dragon King. I believe the reason we lost was that three seals were broken at once, causing the Qilin to appear as part of that chain reaction. Even for someone like Motoyasu, it’s impossible to single-handedly eliminate the Four Spirit Beasts rampaging across various locations. As a result, in that loop, I ended up splitting up from Father and the others to take them down.
“Since the condition was to defeat them all at once, even I had a hard time with it, but I think we can handle it if we organize our forces now.”
A single Guardian Beast is just a pushover, after all. Now that we know how to deal with them, we should be able to finish them off before they trigger a chain reaction.
“All we can do is pray that doesn’t happen. Still… our plan just got derailed all of a sudden.”
“If you want the Nuclear Stones themselves, you can buy them on the market, or I can procure them from the wild.”

“Motoyasu-kun deserves praise for sticking to his policy of not relying on that dragon—who’s supposed to be an acquaintance. Still, even if we were to raise one, whether it could surpass the enemy Dragon Emperor… it seems breaking through its limits would be difficult.”
Father began to ponder further.
“To begin with, Motoyasu, that Rival kid—doesn’t he essentially get ‘overwritten’ whenever he’s near one of our dragons?”
I didn’t quite understand what Father meant, but I don’t lie. I’ll tell you the facts. So, I explained what happened in the instance where Rival passed through my spear.
“In that case, wouldn’t we get a similar result even if we raised him right here? It’s not so much ‘overwriting’ as ‘possession,’ so wouldn’t any dragon do the same if it were close by?”
“That’s true.”

“However… since this world is a loop, that child’s original self still exists, right?　It’s not like they weren’t born, so if we were to pull them in, that child in this world might end up as an empty shell, right?”
“Isn’t worrying about that guy unnecessary? We didn’t need to summon him in the first place.”
There’s no need for that kind of concern. It’s not that we need him—we just need the place he was using. For the sake of my “Eternal Filo-chan” plan, I’ll have Rival disappear.
“I think he’s already dead by now, anyway. So if we raise him, he’ll return from the afterlife.”
“…What do you mean by that?”
Father furrowed his brow and asked for an explanation.

“Well, it’s like this. Rival’s parents were slain by Ren in Melromarc after the first wave of heroes had finished their mission. Shortly after that, adventurers from a nearby village raided the parents’ lair, slaughtering all the monsters. The Assistant was enslaved, and the eggs were taken back and sold off. It seems Rival dies at that time.”
Father pressed his hand to his forehead.
“By the way, a plague breaks out from the dragon’s carcass and strikes the neighboring villages, so it’s a case of karma.”
“It’s Melromarc’s own fault, but it’s still tragic, isn’t it?”
“Foolish… Don’t the people of Melromarc even understand that much?”
The representative of the Shusaku clan said with contempt. The people of that village were greedy, after all. I can’t imagine they had that kind of foresight.
“I heard that Ren fled from Melromarc toward Zeltoble, right? If that’s the case, wouldn’t it make sense for the plague to have spread by now?”
“Since it’s only been a short time since the outbreak, I don’t think it’s become that much of a problem yet.”
At least, based on the timeline, there’s still some leeway before the second wave hits. I think it’s a little earlier than when Father from the first world defeated the dragon zombie.
“That said… in a situation where we’ve run out of options like breaking through limits or boosting our combat strength, having that kid around would probably let us move things along more quickly.”

His necessity is rising to the point where I suspect they’re secretly trying to steer things in that direction behind the scenes. Grrr… I have to talk to him for the sake of the Eternal Filo-chan Project, but it’s an absolute pain.
“The very fact that we have to rely on a dragon is unpleasant, isn’t it, Motoyasu-sama?”
“I suppose so… but this is unavoidable if I’m to fulfill my ambition… Sakura-chan, you’ll just have to bear with it.”
“Hmm?”
Sakura-chan tilts her head, looking a bit dazed.
“A dragon… Nooo~”
She’s reluctant, but she’s still as laid-back as ever. I wonder what it would be like if this were Filo-tan?
“Dragons are the worst!”
She’d be screaming at the top of her lungs, looking right at Father. This contrast… I just can’t seem to reconcile Sakura-chan and Filo-tan in my mind.
“To begin with, since Itsuki isn’t here, we’re the ones who have to quell the unrest in the Melromarc region, aren’t we?”

As for the Four Holy Heroes, Ren is in hiding in Zeltoble, Itsuki died in battle, and the only ones left are me and Father. As for the Seven Star Heroes… the Claw, the Hammer, and the Whip exist in Siltvelt, but their owners are missing. As for the others, aside from the staff held by the Trash, they’re all wanted worldwide under Faubrey’s orders. I’m sure the owner of the gauntlets hasn’t been found yet.
That means the axe and the throwing weapon are still missing. It’s a pretty hopeless situation, isn’t it?
“We can just leave the Melromarc Wave to Trash and the Queen.”
“Well… I guess that’s true.”

Father agrees, glancing at the people of Siltvelt. For the record, we’ve made it appear as though we’ve captured that fake Trash alive. Will that Trash actually be of any use in the Wave? It’s certainly highly doubtful. I still haven’t figured out the conditions for my loop itself. It’s no longer a loop triggered by Ren or Itsuki dying—if defeat in the Wave or something like that is a condition, then we’re out of luck.
“We should go, if only to repay Melromarc a favor. After all, Ms. Eclair worked hard for our sake, too.”

“Ho ho ho, it’s also true that Miss Seaetto went out of her way for us. As allies—and ultimately, for the sake of the future of Siltvelt—it might be a good idea for you Heroes to pay a visit to Melromarc at least once.”
The old man of the Genmu clan agrees. He agreed rather readily—could there be some reason for that? I thought you lot considered Melromarc an enemy nation—what’s the story there?

“The Three Heroes Church has been designated a heretical cult and is in a state of collapse… It would be wise for the Heroes to conduct an inspection for the sake of the future. All the more so if there are those who possess the means to manipulate Shieldfreeden.”

The representative of the Shusaku race also agrees with Father’s policy. So why are you lot—the representative races of Siltvelt—so eager to maintain friendly relations with Melromarc? Hmm… Could it be that? The possibility of the Dragon King’s revival… I heard it would require the sacrifice of two-thirds of the world’s population, so perhaps these fellows are just scared out of their wits.
“That said, Melromarc is the realm ruled by the Wise King and the She-Fox. It’s also true that if we aren’t extremely careful, they’ll exploit any opening… Please be very careful.”
“So, our plan is set. Let’s head to Melromarc as soon as possible… After all, despite everything, we’ve already succeeded in getting back at those who’ve caused us so much trouble.”

In this playthrough, Father was lured out in a carriage on the very first day of the summoning and fell into a trap, didn’t he? There were countless obstacles along the way as well. We made the mastermind behind it all pay, but in the end, Father’s triumphant return to Melromarc will be nothing short of a relentless barrage of harassment.
“I’d also like to say hello to Ms. Eclair… Let’s head to Melromarc.”
“Understood! But…”
I turn my gaze toward Sakura-chan.
“What is it?”
Going to Melromarc means there’s still an issue that’s inextricably linked to Sakura-chan. I’d like to nip that in the bud as much as possible.
“That’s enemy territory. For your safety, Sakura-chan, you should stay behind.”
“Eh?”
Sakura-chan gave me a puzzled look. Father is wearing the exact same expression as Sakura-chan.
“What about Yuki?”
“And Kou?”
“Yuki and Kou will be just fine.”
“Eh? But Sakura can’t come?”
“Why just Sakura?”

That’s a perfectly valid question. It’s because I have a Finacée who’s becoming friends with Filo and Sakura at an incredible speed! …But there’s no way I could ever say that out loud! I’ll have to come up with some excuse to get Sakura-chan to stay home.
“Boo!”
Sakura-chan puffs out her cheeks, angry that she’s been left out. That’s not it at all! It’s my own wish! I simply cannot allow her to get into an inappropriate relationship with my Finacée!

If my Finacée and Filo-tan were just best friends, I wouldn’t say a word. I’d even want them to build a beautiful friendship. But that Finacée is getting all cozy with Filo-tan… How envious… No, I can’t say any more than that. I have to stop that future from happening.
“If it’s dangerous, wouldn’t it be even more helpful to have Sakura-chan there?”
“I’d like to understand your reasoning, Motoyasu-sama… but is Sakura really so useless that she can’t be counted on?”
That’s not true at all! Sakura-chan has done a splendid job protecting Father. I can vouch for that.
“Staying behind… Motoyasu, do you hate Sakura?”
Sakura-chan tilts her little head and stares at me. Suddenly, that gesture overlaps in my mind with the image of Filo-tan, her eyes brimming with tears, pleading with Father. Ugh…
“I love Sakura-chan very much! But it’s dangerous, so you must be very careful! Especially around little girls with blue hair!”

“What’s with that specific detail…? Motoyasu-kun, if you have knowledge of the loops, could you please explain it properly so I know how to handle this? For example, is Sakura-chan killed by that person in Melromarc in every loop?” ”
“She hasn’t been killed.”
“You’re answering that one honestly, aren’t you…? So, in other words, there’s someone in Melromarc who’s extremely inconvenient for you, Motoyasu-kun.”
It seems Father generally understands the situation. Just as I was thinking that, the representative of the Shusaku clan muttered:
“Filolial… and the blue-haired little girl in Melromarc. Could it be…”
Gulp!? I’ve got to get there fast, or Father will get suspicious!
“Well then, let’s get going! Come on! Father, better late than never! Let’s go!”
“Huh? Oh, okay. So—”
No way! I stepped between Father—who was about to speak to the Shusaku representative, who seemed to have an idea—and urged him on.
“We have to hurry or the sun will set! His lair is far away, after all!”
“O-okay, Motoyasu-kun. Let’s get going, then.”
“Yay!”

And so, we ended up heading to Melromarc on short notice. Of course, the regular members are me, Father, Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan. And from Siltvelt, Panda and Zou are coming along as Father’s bodyguards.

Oh, and just so you know, an old man of the Genmu clan is reportedly going to speak with the queen, accompanied by a few attendants, so he’s coming along too. With this group, we immediately used the portal to teleport to Melromarc.
“Hahaha! Wait for me, Mel-chan!”
“Sakura-chan!”

After that, we arrived at Melromarc Castle and requested an audience with the queen. While I took my eyes off Sakura-chan and the others for just a moment, before I knew it, my Finacée was playing with Sakura-chan.
What on earth is going on here!?

I thought I’d been keeping a close watch the whole time, but the moment I shifted my attention to greeting the Queen and the news that Éclairs were on their way—that split-second lapse was exploited, and my Finacée ended up making contact with Sakura-chan. To begin with, Sakura-chan may be laid-back, but she’s incredibly curious. While she was darting around, exploring within my line of sight… she fell prey to my Finacée’s wiles!
“Huh? There’s a child playing with Sakura-chan—I didn’t even notice. Is that one of the noble children visiting the castle?”
“That must be Melty Melromarc, the Second Princess of Melromarc. I believe she came to scout out the Heroes in her capacity as royalty… Ho ho ho, how charming.”
The old man of the Genmu clan seized the moment to explain the situation to Father. Grrr, I thought.
“Her appearance matches the description Motoyasu-kun warned us about earlier to a T.”

Father said this with a subtle expression—part exasperation, part concern. That’s exactly why I warned him. This is my Finacée’s territory… I should’ve been more on guard. I really should’ve insisted on having Sakura-chan stay behind, even if it meant pushing my luck.
“Grrr…”
“She’s having a lot of fun playing tag with Sakura-chan, and Yuki-chan and the others look like they want to join in, too.”
Father walked over toward Sakura-chan and my Finacée. Noticing him approaching, my Finacée snapped back to her senses, lightly adjusted her skirt, and greeted him.
“Good afternoon.”
“G-good afternoon. You’re getting along well with Sakura-chan, aren’t you?”
“Y-yes.”
“Ah, it’d be a big help if you didn’t get too nervous… but I suppose that’s asking too much.”
Well, it is their first meeting, after all. Plus, Father is the Shield Hero. There are certain steps one must take to get along with the Second Princess, who is his Finacée.
“Mel-chan, this is Naofumi. He’s the Hero that Sakura and the others are trying to protect.”
“I see… Judging by the weapon you’re holding, you must be the Shield Hero. My name is Melty—Melromarc…”
“Ah… yeah. I’m Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero who was summoned to this castle a little while ago, and I’ve come for an audience as a representative of Siltvelt.”

“Regarding the Shield Hero and the Spear Hero on this occasion, I apologize for the numerous acts of disrespect committed by the heretical cult in our country, the Three Heroes Church, as well as by impostors posing as Father and older sister… As the Princess of Melromarc, I offer my sincere apologies for this discourtesy.”

My finacée bowed her head politely with a slight nod. So, technically, the Crimson Swine and Trash were considered impostors, weren’t they? No, wait—wasn’t the adventurer named Myne, who was impersonating the Crimson Swine, supposed to have been dealt with?
